surprises.head: The Rangers found the good looks for once
surprises.body: St. Louis is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: the Rangers’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (about 6.1% against St. Louis) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Rangers take down the Blues
paras: Adam Fox struck first for the Rangers early in the second. Oliver Bjorkstrand stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the third, and that one stood up as the winner. The Rangers had a goal taken off for a high stick with just under seven minutes left, though it didn’t end up costing them. Eeli Tolvanen added an empty-net goal with just over two minutes left to make it 3-0, but that didn’t stop St. Louis. Pius Suter got the Blues on the board with just under a minute left.
The Rangers drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Dylan Garand made 32 saves for the Rangers, and Joel Hofer kept the Blues in it, stopping 28 of 30.

Neither power play scored: the Rangers killed all six Blues power plays, and the Blues killed all three of the Rangers’. The Rangers improved to 8-7-1 and climbed to third in the Metropolitan, while the Blues dropped to 7-7-1, slipping to sixth in the Central.

items.text: The Rangers won for the first time in five games.
Pavel Dorofeyev’s five-game point streak ended.
Pius Suter is now one goal from 100.
